claim: A torch decoration (type 30) can be put out by a wire, but a candle decoration keeps its flame whatever its state.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/view.cpp:2930-2936 (viewProcessSprites, case kDecorationTorch: no XSPRITE or state 1 draws picnum+1 and the high torch effect, otherwise smoke)

NBlood/source/blood/src/view.cpp:2922-2929 (case kDecorationCandle: no XSPRITE or state 1 gives shade -128 and kViewEffectPhase, otherwise shade -8) and :2360-2373 (kViewEffectPhase adds tile 626 at the sprite's top, shade 26); types at common_game.h:239-240
use: Use type 30 or 32 for fires that a rite or switch puts out, with LampGroup for the light they give; a candle that must never go dark is a plain decoration or a type 32 with no XSPRITE.
instead: Both can be put out. A torch (type 30) draws picnum+1 with the high torch effect while its state is 1 and smoke otherwise; a candle (kDecorationCandle, type 32) is drawn at shade -128 with a flame sprite (tile 626, itself at shade 26) over its top while its state is 1, and at shade -8 without it otherwise. One of either type with no XSPRITE is always lit, and so is a plain decoration whose tile shows a flame.

checked.how: view.cpp:2920-2936 (viewProcessSprites) read: kDecorationCandle with no XSPRITE or state 1 gets shade -128 and kViewEffectPhase, else shade -8; kDecorationTorch with no XSPRITE or state 1 draws picnum+1 and kViewEffectTorchHigh, else kViewEffectSmokeHigh. view.cpp:2360-2373: kViewEffectPhase inserts tile 626 at the sprite's top at shade 26, repeat 24.
